subject: Cross-functional OKR synthesis and one-line narratives for QBR
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Cross-functional OKR synthesis and one-line narratives for QBR

Team —

As we lock the QBR narrative next week, I want to collect two things from each functional lead by Thursday EOD: (1) final OKR scores using the attached scoring template, and (2) a 1-2 sentence narrative we can put verbatim in the leadership slide deck (what changed this quarter and why the score is what it is).

Guidance for scoring:
- 0.0–0.4: Miss — significant scope or execution shortfall
- 0.5–0.7: Partial — good progress but missed our key result(s)
- 0.8–1.0: Meet/Exceed — delivered the outcome with measurable impact

Please pay special attention to the "customer reliability" objective — we need numbers (latency p95, incidents, cost impact) not just qualitative statements. I started a synthesis doc here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1QBR_OKR_Synthesis_Doc — drop your narratives inline.

I've attached a blank scoring sheet to make aggregation easy. If you have a heatmap or supporting artifact, attach it to your reply.

Thanks — I'll stitch this into the draft narrative on Friday and share a version for review.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & Platform
Redwood Inference
[attachment: QBR_OKR_Scoring_Template.xlsx (Spreadsheet, 78KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-functional OKR synthesis and one-line narratives for QBR

Vivek —

Thanks for the clear ask. Draft scores attached (I filled sections for Growth & GTM). High level: 0.8 for Acquisition (we hit MQL targets and two pilot expansions), 0.6 for Activation (onboarding funnel still leaky at step 2), and note about churn in segment B — see comments in the sheet.

One-line narrative (drop-in): "GTM delivered predictable acquisition velocity this quarter and closed two strategic pilots; activation conversion remains the primary lever for unlocking revenue scale."

Attachment: Eng leadership asked for more detail on reliability metrics before we finalize the customer-facing narrative — looping Karthik.

Laura Bennett
Head of Growth
Redwood Inference
[attachment: QBR_OKR_Scoring_Template.xlsx (filled, 22KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-functional OKR synthesis and one-line narratives for QBR

Vivek / Laura —

Quick notes from infra/eng: I've uploaded a heatmap that shows percentage of traffic served from cache vs uncached and the KV hit-rate deltas month-over-month (see eng-team-heatmap.pdf). For OKR scoring I propose: Reliability objective 0.7 (partial) — we reduced p95 by 12% but had two tier-3 incidents during the big release window.

Question: do we want to normalize scoring for org headcount changes? We had a smaller platform team in Q1 and regained two ICs mid-Q2 which materially affected throughput. If we normalize, the reliability score moves to 0.8. Happy to follow whichever convention leadership prefers — propose we annotate the scoring sheet with "headcount-normalized" flags so reviewers can see the adjustment.

One-line narrative: "Platform improvements reduced tail latency and increased cache density, though incident remediation during the release window limited full attainment of our reliability target."

Karthik Iyer
VP Engineering, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
[attachment: eng-team-heatmap.pdf (PDF, 140KB)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-functional OKR synthesis and one-line narratives for QBR

Thanks Karthik — good context.

Decision: keep the raw scores but add a second column for "normalized" scores with a one-sentence justification when applicable. That preserves transparency and lets execs see both views. Karthik, please add the normalized numbers in the same sheet and add a tiny note about the staffing variance. Laura, please update your growth numbers with a short callout about the pilot ARR that you mentioned (we'll need that for the revenue slide).

I'll consolidate on Thursday morning and circulate a single slide deck for comments. Two requests for everyone:
1) Limit narratives to two lines max — we will edit for voice, we need concise signal.
2) If you reference numbers (p95, ARR, churn %), put the source in the doc as a link or a HubSpot record id.

Also: OpsConsulting is still running the customer interviews next week; Maria Lopez from Acme is on the results call on Wednesday — if any OKR narrative is customer-facing, please flag it.

Vivek
